question: A team wants every developer who clones a repository to get the same build commands and architecture notes in Claude Code. Where should this guidance live?
optionA: A CLAUDE.md committed to the repo
optionB: A CLAUDE.local.md in the repo root
explanation: A project CLAUDE.md is shared through source control, so everyone who clones gets it. CLAUDE.local.md is personal, and anything under ~/.claude stays on one machine.

question: A developer wants Claude to know a personal sandbox URL, but only in this project and never in version control. Which file fits best?
explanation: CLAUDE.local.md holds personal, project-specific notes and belongs in .gitignore. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md would apply the note to every project, and the other two are committed for the whole team.

question: A monorepo has CLAUDE.md files at the root, in packages/api and in packages/web. A session starts in packages/api. Which files load at launch?
optionD: Only the file at the root
explanation: Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md from the working directory and every directory above it at launch. Files in other parts of the tree, like packages/web, are not ancestors and do not load at launch.

question: Two CLAUDE.md files loaded in one session give contradictory formatting instructions. How does Claude Code resolve this?
optionA: The file nearest the working directory overrides
optionB: The file at the repository root overrides
optionC: Startup stops and reports a settings error
optionD: Both stay in context; either may be followed
explanation: Discovered files are concatenated rather than overriding each other, so Claude may pick either instruction when they conflict. The fix is to review the files and remove the contradiction.

question: A team splits an 800-line CLAUDE.md into several files pulled in with @ imports, hoping to reduce context use on every task. What will they find?
optionA: Context cost stays about the same
optionB: Imported files load only on demand
optionC: Imported files load only in subagents
optionD: Imported text is summarized on load
explanation: Imported files are expanded and load together with the CLAUDE.md that references them, so imports organize a file without reducing its cost. Path-scoped rules or skills are what defer loading.

question: API conventions matter only when Claude works on files under src/api, and the team wants them out of context the rest of the time. What is the best home for them?
optionA: An @ import in the root CLAUDE.md file
optionB: A .claude/rules file with a paths field
optionC: A section in the root CLAUDE.md file
explanation: A rule with paths frontmatter loads only when Claude works with matching files. An @ import or a CLAUDE.md section loads every session, and a hook is for running commands rather than holding guidance.

question: A CLAUDE.md line says never to read a credentials file, and the security lead needs that to hold every time, whatever the model decides. What should the team do?
optionA: Rewrite the line in capital letters
optionC: Add a Read deny rule for the file
optionD: Import the line from a policy file
explanation: CLAUDE.md is context that Claude weighs, not enforced configuration, so stronger wording gives no guarantee. Claude Code applies deny rules itself in every permission mode. They cover file tools and commands like cat, but not a script that opens the file, so add the sandbox for OS-level coverage.

question: A committed .claude/settings.json turns an option on. One developer wants it off for herself in this project, without affecting teammates. Where should she set it?
explanation: Project local settings sit above shared project settings and stay personal. User settings rank below shared project settings, so the committed value would still win there.

question: A security team needs a tool restriction on every developer machine that nobody can override in their own files or with a command-line flag. Where does it belong?
explanation: Managed settings hold the top precedence, above the command line and every settings file. A managed CLAUDE.md is guidance Claude weighs, not technical enforcement, so tool restrictions go in settings.

question: User settings and shared project settings each define a permissions.allow list. Which rules apply in a session in that project?
optionA: Only the rules from the project list
optionC: Only the rules from the user list
optionD: Whichever list has the most rules
explanation: List keys such as permissions.allow merge across settings files rather than overriding. Each file can add entries without removing another file's.

question: Settings contain a deny rule Bash(aws *) and an allow rule Bash(aws s3 ls). Claude tries to run aws s3 ls. What happens?
optionA: It runs; the narrower rule wins
optionB: It prompts; the two rules conflict
optionC: It is blocked; deny is checked first
optionD: It runs if allow is in local settings
explanation: Rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow, and specificity does not change that order. An allow rule cannot carve an exception out of a deny rule, whichever settings file holds it.

question: A team wants git diff commands to run without a prompt, but the rule must not also match git diff-index. Which allow rule fits?
explanation: The space before the trailing wildcard is part of the rule, so it stops at the word boundary. Without the space the rule also matches git diff-index, and git * allows every git command.

question: A deny rule Bash(curl *) is meant to keep Claude's shell commands off the internet, but it misses forms like sh -c 'curl ...'. What enforces the limit reliably?
optionA: The sandbox with a network allowlist
optionC: An allow rule for WebFetch domains
optionD: A CLAUDE.md line that bans curl use
explanation: Bash rules match command text, so the same program invoked another way slips past them. The sandbox enforces network limits at the OS level for shell commands, whatever the command text says.

question: In the terminal, a developer picks "Yes, and don't ask again" when Claude runs npm test. Who does the saved approval affect?
optionB: Only that developer, in that repository
optionD: Nobody, since it ends with the session
explanation: The approval is saved as an allow rule in .claude/settings.local.json, which is personal and kept out of commits. Only file-edit approvals end with the session; a Bash approval persists for that repository.

question: A teammate opens a repo for the first time in an interactive session. Its committed settings hold allow and deny rules, and she has not accepted the trust dialog. Which rules apply?
optionA: Allow rules only, until she trusts it
optionB: Both sets, as soon as the session opens
optionC: Deny rules only, until she trusts it
optionD: Neither set, until she trusts the folder
explanation: Allow rules grant capability, so they wait for workspace trust. Deny and ask rules only restrict, so they apply right away.

question: A team wants all Bash commands to run without prompts, except a few its own script identifies as dangerous. Which setup fits best?
optionA: Allow Bash; block with a PostToolUse hook
optionB: Allow Bash; name the risks in CLAUDE.md
optionC: Deny Bash; approve with a Stop hook script
optionD: Allow Bash; block with a PreToolUse hook
explanation: A blocking PreToolUse hook stops the call before it runs, even when an allow rule would permit it. PostToolUse fires after the command has already run, and CLAUDE.md is not enforced.

question: A PreToolUse command hook must stop a call and tell Claude why. Using exit codes alone, what should the script do?
optionA: Exit 2 with the reason on stderr
optionB: Exit 1 with the reason on stderr
optionC: Exit 0 with the reason on stderr
optionD: Exit 2 with the reason on stdout
explanation: Exit code 2 blocks the action and the stderr text becomes the reason. Exit 1 is a non-blocking error, so the action still proceeds.

question: A PreToolUse hook returns a permissionDecision of allow for a command that also matches a deny rule in settings. What is the result?
optionA: The hook's allow overrides the rule
optionB: The deny rule still blocks the call
optionC: The user is prompted to pick a side
optionD: The hook's allow applies this one time
explanation: Hook decisions do not bypass permission rules: deny and ask rules are evaluated regardless of what a PreToolUse hook returns. A hook can tighten restrictions but cannot loosen them past the rules.

question: A team wants its formatter to run after every file Claude changes, without relying on Claude to remember. Which configuration fits best?
explanation: A PostToolUse hook runs right after the matched tool, and Claude Code runs it whether or not Claude remembers. A PreToolUse hook would format the file before the edit lands.

question: Claude sometimes ends its turn with type errors in the code. The team wants the turn not to finish until the typecheck passes. What should they configure?
optionA: A SessionStart hook that runs the check
optionB: A CLAUDE.md line requiring the check
optionC: A PostToolUse hook logging the result
optionD: A Stop hook that exits 2 on failure
explanation: A Stop hook runs when Claude tries to finish, and exit 2 sends Claude back to work with the stderr output as the reason. A CLAUDE.md line works most of the time but is not enforced. A cap ends the turn after eight blocks in a row with no tool call.

question: A 40-step release procedure in CLAUDE.md is used twice a month but takes up context in every session. What is the best change?
optionA: Move it into a project skill
optionB: Move it into an @ imported file
optionD: Move it into a SessionStart hook
explanation: A skill's body loads only when it is used, which suits long, occasional procedures. Imported files and CLAUDE.local.md load every session, as does SessionStart output.

question: A /deploy skill has real side effects, and it should run only when a person types the command, never because Claude judged it relevant. Which frontmatter achieves this?
explanation: disable-model-invocation stops Claude from loading the skill by itself, leaving manual invocation. user-invocable: false does the reverse, hiding it from the menu so only Claude can use it.

question: A deep-research skill produces long output the team does not want in the main conversation. Its instructions are self-contained. Which frontmatter fits best?
optionD: paths, limited to the research folder
explanation: context: fork runs the skill in an isolated subagent, and agent picks which type, such as Explore. A forked skill does not see the conversation, which is why its instructions must stand alone.

question: A developer's personal skill and a repository's project skill share the name lint. Which one does a session in that repository use?
explanation: For skills, enterprise overrides personal and personal overrides project. Subagents work the other way round, where the project definition beats the user one.

question: A team needs a reviewer subagent that cannot edit files, enforced by Claude Code and not merely requested in a prompt. What should its definition include?
explanation: The tools field is an allowlist that Claude Code enforces, so a subagent without an editing tool cannot edit. Instructions in its prompt only shape what it tries to do.

question: Claude has spent ten turns diagnosing an auth bug and now delegates the fix to a fresh custom subagent. How does the subagent learn the findings?
optionB: Claude must include them in the task
optionC: It reads them from auto memory
optionD: It sees the files Claude has read
explanation: A non-fork subagent starts fresh, without the conversation history or the files Claude already read, and auto memory does not carry over. It works from the delegation message Claude writes.

question: Several custom refactoring subagents will edit overlapping files in parallel. Which frontmatter setting keeps their edits from colliding?
explanation: With isolation set to worktree, each subagent works in its own temporary git worktree with a separate copy of the repository. Running in the background changes timing, not which files are shared.

question: A developer is about to change an unfamiliar module and wants to review Claude's proposal before any source file is touched. How should she start the session?
explanation: In plan mode Claude reads files and explores but makes no edits until the plan is approved. acceptEdits does the opposite, writing files without asking.

question: A team wants one internal MCP server available to everyone who clones the repository, defined in version control. Which option fits best?
optionB: claude mcp add, with no scope flag
explanation: Project scope writes the server to .mcp.json in the repo root, which is committed and shared. Local is the default and stays private to one developer, and user scope follows one person across projects.

question: A committed .mcp.json points at a remote server that needs a bearer token. How should the token reach the server?
optionA: The literal token in the headers block
optionC: A token in a committed .env file
optionD: A token in the root CLAUDE.md file
explanation: Project configuration is visible in version control, so secrets should not be committed. Environment variable expansion in headers lets each person or job supply the value at run time.

question: A CI job must use only the MCP server defined in ci-mcp.json and ignore the servers in the repository's .mcp.json. Which flags fit?
explanation: --strict-mcp-config limits the session to servers passed with --mcp-config. Non-interactive runs otherwise load project servers without prompting, so --mcp-config alone can leave them connected.

question: A CI step needs Claude's reply to match a specific JSON Schema so that a later step can parse it. Which approach fits best with claude -p?
explanation: --output-format json with --json-schema returns conforming data in the structured_output field. Asking for a format in a prompt leaves it to the model, and the script should still check the field is present.

question: A locked-down CI job should run only tools it has pre-approved, and anything else that would prompt must be refused. Which permission mode fits?
explanation: dontAsk denies every call that would otherwise prompt, while pre-approved tools and actions that need no approval still run. auto has a classifier judge actions instead of following a fixed list.

question: A script runs several claude -p conversations side by side and must send a follow-up to one particular conversation. What is the reliable way?
explanation: --output-format json returns a session_id that --resume can target. --continue only picks the most recent conversation, which may not be the one the script means when runs overlap.

question: A workflow using claude-code-action should review each pull request when it is opened, with nobody typing @claude. How should it be configured?
optionA: Set trigger_phrase to the PR title
optionB: Set allowed_bots to the PR author
optionD: Set github_token to an OAuth token
explanation: With a prompt input the action runs in automation mode, on the workflow's event, without waiting for a mention. With no prompt it stays in interactive mode and waits for the trigger phrase.

question: A scheduled workflow gives claude-code-action a plain-text prompt that needs GitHub data, but Claude reports it cannot reach the API. What is the most likely fix?
optionA: Run checkout with a deeper fetch-depth first
optionB: Mention @claude inside of the prompt text
optionC: Describe the API in the repo's CLAUDE.md
explanation: For a plain-text prompt in automation mode, Claude has no shell or GitHub API access until the tools are granted. They can be granted through --allowedTools in claude_args or an allow rule in the settings input.

question: A developer wants one Claude session building a feature and another fixing a bug at the same time, with no risk of their file edits colliding. Which setup fits best?
optionB: Two claude sessions in one checkout
optionC: Two subagents with no isolation set
explanation: Each worktree is a separate checkout on its own branch, so edits cannot collide while history stays shared. Sessions or subagents in one checkout all edit the same files.

question: Sessions started with claude --worktree keep failing because the gitignored .env file the app needs is missing. What is the best fix?
explanation: A worktree is a fresh checkout, so untracked files are absent. Files that match .worktreeinclude and are also gitignored get copied into each new worktree, without putting secrets in git.

question: A long session has just written a rate limiter. The team wants a review that is not swayed by the reasoning that produced the code. What fits best?
optionA: Ask the same session to recheck the diff
optionB: Run /compact, then ask for a full review
optionC: Review it in a fresh session or subagent
optionD: Raise the effort in the same conversation
explanation: A reviewer that never saw the conversation is not influenced by how the code was written. Staying in the same session keeps that reasoning in context, even after compaction summarizes it.

question: A developer has corrected Claude twice on the same problem, and the result is still wrong. What is the best next step?
explanation: A third correction adds to a conversation that already holds two failed attempts for Claude to re-read. Starting clean with one prompt that folds in what was learned usually works better.
